messages:
maria_sales: Quick sync 0: ACME says POC approved but finance/procurement won't sign until we resolve three items on the order form: IP wording for connectors, SLA target during POC, and multi-entity signing flow. Link: https://drive.google.com/ACME-POC-OF (ref: OF-ACME-42). Can legal/procurement triage?

 dan_ae: They explicitly wrote that any integrations built during the POC are their property. Wants that in writing.

 rachel_se: Practically the POC outputs are prompts + infra config and we do not ship source code. We should agree to a narrow license for the POC runtime only.

 chris_legal: Paste the customer's exact redline please. Also are they asking for perpetual ownership or just for the POC artifacts?

 maria_sales: Customer redline: "All integrations, connectors, and derivative works produced during the evaluation period shall be owned solely by Customer. Vendor shall have no rights to such assets."

 vijay_procure: Procurement also flagged billing: need PO reference, remittance address, and whether they require a separate contractor invoice for each BU. Also multi-entity signing: BU1 wants to sign first, BU2 countersigns.

 chris_legal: Draft alternative: "Customer retains ownership of Customer-developed connectors and configurations. Vendor is granted a limited, revocable license to execute and validate such connectors solely for the duration of the POC and for the purpose of providing the evaluation. Vendor may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvements."

 rachel_se: Add auto-expiry 30 days post-POC for the license. No ongoing rights to reuse connector code.

 elaine_csm: For DocuSign: we support multiple signer flows and conditional routing. Need final signer emails and which entity signs first. CSM can set template.

 vijay_procure: On the SLA: ACME wants 99.9% availability for POC. Our standard non-production is 99.5. Procurement prefers credits instead of raising the SLO. Also need limitation on work we commit to during the POC.

 chris_legal: Proposed POC SLA compromise: "Vendor uses commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.7% availability during the POC. Customer may claim service credits equal to 7% of the monthly fee for each month availability falls below 99.7%, capped at 35% per month."

 dan_ae: Customer signaled they prefer 99.9 but will accept credits instead. We need a quick yes/no.

 vijay_procure: Suggest lowering the credit exposure: 5% per month, cap at 25%. Minimizes risk.

 chris_legal: I'll float 7%/35% as middle ground to Legal Ops; willing to tweak cap if Procurement insists.

 security_bot: Security task: ACME's vendor questionnaire asks about KMS and SOC2 scope. Ticket SEC-2024-88. SE note: POC will use vendor-managed KMS unless we do a private deployment; customer asked if we can use their key.

 rachel_se: Not realistic to switch to customer KMS for a two-week POC. Recommend we provide encryption details, SOC2 attestation, and an offer to integrate customer-managed KMS in onboarding for paid deployment.

 maria_sales: Action items: (1) @chris_legal post redline for IP + SLA by 3pm PT, (2) @dan_ae gather signer names/emails + PO number, (3) @vijay_procure confirm remittance details and whether separate invoices needed.

 vijay_procure: Procurement can approve DocuSign template once legal posts final order form. Send final PDF and signer emails to procurement@redwood.com. Include PO in the subject.

 chris_legal: I'll upload a redline and leave comments about the license scope and SLA credits. Will cc Legal Ops on signature routing.

 dan_ae: I'll get signer list and PO from the customer and drop here by EOD.

 elaine_csm: I'll prepare the DocuSign template draft and keep it on standby.

 maria_sales: Great 0: thanks team. Please tag the customer with #escalate once redline is ready so they can review and sign. Closing once countersigned. :white_check_mark:
